
{{alias}}( order, M, N, A, LDA, TAU, WORK, LWORK )
    Computes an LQ factorization of a real M-by-N matrix A:

    If LWORK = -1, the routine only calculates the optimal
    size of the WORK array, returns this value as the first entry of WORK,
    and exits with info = 0.

    Indexing is relative to the first index. To introduce an offset, use typed
    array views.

    Parameters
    ----------
    order: string
        Storage layout. Must be either 'row-major' or 'column-major'.

    M: integer
        Number of rows in the matrix A. Must be a nonnegative integer.

    N: integer
        Number of columns in the matrix A. Must be a nonnegative integer.

    A: Float64Array
        Input/output matrix. On input, the M-by-N matrix A. On output, the
        elements on and below the diagonal contain the M-by-min(M,N) lower
        trapezoidal matrix L; the elements above the diagonal contain the
        vectors v defining the elementary reflectors. At least `LDA * max(1,N)`
        elements for row-major, `LDA * max(1,M)` for column-major.

    LDA: integer
        Stride of the first dimension of A (a.k.a., leading dimension).
        For column-major, LDA >= max(1,M). For row-major, LDA >= max(1,N).

    TAU: Float64Array
        Output array for scalar factors of elementary reflectors.
        Length must be at least `min(M,N)`.

    WORK: Float64Array
        Workspace array. For optimal performance, `LWORK >= M*NB` where NB is
        the optimal block size. If `LWORK = -1`, a workspace query is assumed;
        the optimal size is returned in `WORK[0]` and no computation is
        performed.

    LWORK: integer
        Dimension of the array WORK.

    Returns
    -------
    info: integer
        Status code. 0 indicates success.

    Examples
    --------
    > var A = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}([1,5,9,2,6,10,3,7,11,4,8,12]);
    > var TAU = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 3 );
    > var WORK = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 4 );
    > {{alias}}( 'column-major', 3, 4, A, 3, TAU, WORK, 4 )
    0
    > A
    <Float64Array>[~-5.477,~-12.78,~-20.083,~0.309,~-3.266,~-6.532,~0.463,~-0.327,~0.0,~0.618,~-0.789,~0.618]
    > TAU
    <Float64Array>[ ~1.183, ~1.156, ~1.447 ]
    > WORK
    <Float64Array>[ 3.0, ~24.593, 0.0, 0.0 ]


{{alias}}.ndarray( M, N, A,sA1,sA2,oA, TAU,sTAU,oTAU, WORK,sWORK,oWORK, LWORK )
    Computes an LQ factorization of a real M-by-N matrix A using alternative
    indexing semantics.

    Parameters
    ----------
    M: integer
        Number of rows in the matrix A. Must be a nonnegative integer.

    N: integer
        Number of columns in the matrix A. Must be a nonnegative integer.

    A: Float64Array
        Input/output matrix.

    sA1: integer
        Stride of the first dimension of A.

    sA2: integer
        Stride of the second dimension of A.

    oA: integer
        Starting index for A.

    TAU: Float64Array
        Output array for scalar factors of elementary reflectors.

    sTAU: integer
        Stride for TAU.

    oTAU: integer
        Starting index for TAU.

    WORK: Float64Array
        Workspace array.

    sWORK: integer
        Stride for WORK array.

    oWORK: integer
        Starting index for WORK.

    LWORK: integer
        Dimension of the array WORK.

    Returns
    -------
    info: integer
        Status code. 0 indicates success.

    Examples
    --------
    > var A = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}([1,5,9,2,6,10,3,7,11,4,8,12]);
    > var TAU = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 3 );
    > var WORK = new {{alias:@stdlib/array/float64}}( 4 );
    > {{alias}}.ndarray( 3, 4, A, 1, 3, 0, TAU, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0, 4 )
    0
    > A
    <Float64Array>[~-5.477,~-12.78,~-20.083,~0.309,~-3.266,~-6.532,~0.463,~-0.327,~0.0,~0.618,~-0.789,~0.618]
    > TAU
    <Float64Array>[ ~1.183, ~1.156, ~1.447 ]
    > WORK
    <Float64Array>[ 3.0, ~24.593, 0.0, 0.0 ]

    See Also
    --------
